note: doc/phase3_6_tasks_and_acceptance.md section 6. Ten packages, thirty standards. Section 8 is explicit about what the sign-off does NOT mean: not that an FPGA runs, not that an ASIC is implemented, not that the project is production-signed.

packages.title: backend abstraction and the direction of dependency
the shared RTL and a complete export
storage, clock and reset adaptation boundaries
the host protocol, completion and recovery
the shared conformance suite and the regression gate
downstream handoff and the extension rehearsal

A.may_then_claim: the engineering boundary and the compatibility rules are frozen

B.may_then_claim: the shared hardware and host interfaces are verified through a reference adapter

C.may_then_claim: the mainline can be handed to an independent platform branch

claim_levels.note: Section 3.2. These are not interchangeable and each has to be recorded as itself.
claim_levels.operational: the existing simulated execution, with its tested range stated
claim_levels.integration-tested: a reference adapter other than the built-in binding, closed through real RTL or a protocol loop to it. NOT a claim that a board ran anything.
claim_levels.engineering-ready: the shared package and interfaces exist and are tested; the specific platform is NOT verified
claim_levels.platform-verified: reserved. Nothing in this stage may claim it.

mutations.what: return a reply under the wrong epoch
report completion before the writes are visible
drop a dependency from the export
forge a PASS or hide a missing case

budget.note: Section 5.2: frozen at the start, measured from the small tests that already exist, never guessed from an imagined platform. RTL is slow, so a single run registry serves several checks.

workload_caps.note: Section 5.1: reuse the small workloads. No new large models, no whole-machine sweeps, no RTL benchmark growth for the sake of looking board-ready.

fidelity.note: Section 5.2: on the same hardware implementation, pure engineering refactoring may not change the machine code or the device cycles of R3.5's frozen workloads. A necessary semantic change is identified separately and gets its own regression and performance evidence; it is not folded into a directory move called 'no behaviour change'.
